title: 'Saral' way to start an industry in Kerala in just 75 days, SARAL Keralam Act, 2026, passed in Assembly
content: The SARAL (Simplified & Accelerated Regulatory Approvals and Licensing) Keralam Act, 2026, which provides for the constitution of a statutory authority to grant licences and clearances for projects over 25 crore, was passed in the Assembly on Friday. The statutory authority will be called the SARAL Keralam Authority, and its brief under the new law is to issue an 'Integrated Enterprise Clearance Certificate' to an investor by, in the words of industries minister PK Kunhalikutty, "accelerating the process of obtaining various licences, clearances, permits and approvals from various government authorities under various laws for the establishment, operation, expansion, diversification or modernisation of investment projects with a capital investment exceeding 25 crore". The Authority will have to grant clearances in two and a half months, within seventy-five days. For the implementation of the Act, relevant sections and rules related to 19 state laws will be amended. The Act, however, will not have any influence over clearances that are governed by central laws. The driving principle of the Act is 'One State – One Approval – One Document'. From now on, the investor will deal only with the SARAL Keralam Authority and not with various government departments. Tyranny of bureaucracy Instead of separate applications for each government department involved in the vetting of the project proposal, an investor will need to submit only one application for all the necessary clearances. And this has to be submitted to the SARAL Secretariat through the Portal (the common online portal created for the receipt, processing, tracking and disposal of applications) or in physical mode. If defects or deficiencies are spotted, the departments will not be allowed to point them out separately, but all the issues flagged by the concerned departments will have to be collected together and then conveyed. In other words, the departments have been stripped of their authority to ask for documents at spaced-out intervals that can frustrate the applicant and delay the project inordinately. What's more, these defects can be informed only to the SARAL Secretariat and not to the applicants, as is done now. The Secretariat, then, will issue to the applicant what the Act calls a 'Consolidated Defect Memo'. In short, the new law will obviate the investor's self-degrading compulsion to run after officers of individual departments like KSEB or Water Authority or the Panchayat. However, the right of government departments to carry out inspections or enforce compliance has not been taken away. It is just that the power to suspend or revoke a licence has been transferred exclusively to the Approval Committee. SARAL structures Under the Act, there will be a two-tier statutory clearance mechanism at the State-level and the district-level. At the state-level, there will be the State Level Referral-cum-Appraisal Committee and the State Level Approval Committee. These will deal with all investments above 25 crore. The Referral-cum-Appraisal Committee will be chaired by the industries secretary and will have more than nine members, including a senior officer from the Chief Secretary's office. On receiving an application from the SARAL Secretariat, this Referral-cum-Appraisal Committee will evaluate the application, convene meetings with concerned departments, resolve discrepancies, if any, between the departments, and submit a consolidated report, detailing why the clearance was either granted or withheld, to the State-Level Approval Committee for the final decision. The Approval Committee will be chaired by the Chief Secretary and will have nine members, mostly secretaries of various government departments like industries, finance, revenue, law, programme implementation and information and public relations. Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation (KSIDC) Managing Director will be the convenor. The Approval Committee has the power to grant or deny clearance...
